events.name: An Evening With RAYE
events.description:
Moderated by the CEO of The Recording Academy Harvey Mason Jr.

The Grammy Museum is thrilled to welcome four-time Grammy Award-nominated singer, songwriter and producer RAYE to the Museum's Ray Charles Rooftop Terrace for an evening discussing her newest critically acclaimed album, THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE., her creative process, career, and more, with a special performance. Attendees will have an opportunity to enjoy rooftop views, a café with food, and a cash bar prior to the program.
Honored with the Recording Academy’s 2026 Harry Belafonte Best Song For Social Change CEO Merit Award, RAYE has charted 21 Top 40 UK singles and amassed over 10 billion streams on Spotify alone since her 2014 debut. In 2024, the South London native made UK music history at the BRIT Awards by winning six trophies in a single night—the most by any artist—including Album of the Year and becoming the first woman ever named Songwriter of the Year. Shortlisted for the 2023 and 2026 Mercury Prizes, RAYE also became the first artist in Recording Academy history to earn simultaneous GRAMMY nods for Best New Artist and Songwriter of the Year (Non-Classical) in the same year.
RAYE’s independent sophomore album, THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE. (Human Re Sources/The Orchard), made an immediate impact upon release, marking her first UK No. 1 album, her highest Billboard 200 debut, and reaching the Top 10 across 16 territories. Defying genre and industry norms, the project continues to resonate with audiences around the globe while highlighting her artistic evolution. Written, composed, produced, and arranged by RAYE, the 17-track LP spans four distinct "seasons" and features 170 live musicians. The project includes the inescapable smash hit “WHERE IS MY HUSBAND!,” which premiered at Glastonbury, has since surpassed 1.5 billion streams, and is now certified RIAA Double Platinum. Ranking on countless Best Albums of 2026 mid-year lists, additional highlights include the soaring ballads “Nightingale Lane.” and “I Know You’re Hurting.,” alongside notable collaborations with GRAMMY winners Hans Zimmer (“Click Clack Symphony.”) and Al Green (“Goodbye Henry.”). The LP also features guest appearances by RAYE's sisters Amma and Absolutely (“Joy.”), contributions from the London Symphony Orchestra (conducted by Tom Richards) and the Flames Collective Choir, as well as production by Mike Sabath, Tom Richards, Chris Hill, Pete Clements, Jordan Riley, and Punctual.Recently featured on the cover of Billboard’s May issue highlighting her breakthrough as an independent artist, RAYE became the first British woman to receive the Songwriters Hall of Fame Hal David Starlight Award, joining past honorees Taylor Swift, SZA, and Alicia Keys. Her accolades also include an MTV Video Music Award, Ivor Novello Awards for Songwriter of the Year and the Songwriter Advocate Award, and 2026 nominations at the MTV VMAs, BET Awards, AMAs, and iHeartRadio Music Awards.
RAYE spent early 2026 performing THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE. to sold-out arenas across Europe and the UK—including six sold-out nights at London’s The O2—before a sold-out North American trek featuring multiple nights at Radio City Music Hall and the Greek Theatre. She is currently touring as a special guest on Bruno Mars’ The Romantic Tour, performing across 24 North American stadiums.
For tickets and more information, visit RAYEofficial.com. THIS MUSIC MAY CONTAIN HOPE. is available on all platforms.

events.name: Los Angeles Coliseum Historic Tours
events.info: Our comprehensive, educational tour will entertain you with the historical significance of the Coliseum, while highlighting recent renovations and the future of this internationally recognized venue. You will embark on a 75-minute walking tour, which includes a view into the elegant ambience of the Founders Suites and breathtaking views of the Los Angeles skyline from the 1923 Club rooftop deck atop the Scholarship Club Tower. You will have a special opportunity to experience the game day of an athlete, spending time in the locker room and running through the Players Tunnel onto the playing field. Photos and videos are welcome! The tour ends inside of the classic seating bowl, following in the footsteps of the worlds greatest athletes and entertainers to the iconic Peristyle. You will walk under the Coliseum Torch and absorb the historical impact of those enshrined in the Coliseum Court of Honor. We are excited for you to tour the Greatest Stadium in the World
events.pleaseNote: Tours start promptly at scheduled time. Enter at Gate 33A. Please note: This is a walking tour. Tour schedule, route, stops and activities are subject to change without notice. Parking is available in Exposition Park's Blue Structure at 550 Exposition Park Dr. The Metro E-Line also services Exposition Park, use Expo Park/USC station. Enter the Coliseum at the Coliseum Welcome Center located at Gate 33A.
